question: Up 3 in the last 12 seconds, should the leader foul or defend?
answer: Foul. The leader wins 93.6% of the time fouling and 92.4% defending, +2.8 points at equal time (CI +0.8 to +4.6).
findings: Leader win rate: 93.6% fouling (CI 92.0%-94.9%, n=1063) and 92.4% defending (CI 91.7%-93.1%, n=6053).
The difference at the same time left (foul minus defend) is +2.8 points (95% CI +0.8 to +4.6).
The game reached OT 6.7% of the time after a foul and 14.2% after defending. The leader lost in regulation 3.1% and 0.9% of the time.
Once in OT, the leader won 50.7% after fouling (n=71) and 52.7% after defending (n=857).
method: The sample is the first trailing-team possession of each game that is live with 12 seconds or less left in the final regulation period, down 3. A foul is the leader's non-shooting foul that sends the trailing team to the line before any shot. Fouling and defending are compared within possession-start bins (4-8, 8-12, 12+ s), and the outcome is the game win, including OT.
data: ESPN play-by-play via sportsdataverse, CBB, 2011-12 to 2025-26, 7,116 games.
split_check: Foul minus defend was +2.2 points in 2012-19 (CI -0.6 to +4.8) and +3.3 in 2020-26 (CI +0.7 to +5.8).
